title: Request stew & priority bubble — compact customer synth
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, intentionally messy roll-up of customer feedback we've collected across support threads, field interviews, and direct engineering syncs (Nov 1–Nov 17). Use it as a quick scout for low-effort fixes, mid-term feature lanes, and risk flags that should bubble to product/infra. Not a polished roadmap — think stew: lots in, extract a few strong flavors.

Snapshot (one-liners):
- Top emergent theme: customers want predictable p95/p99 latency guarantees and easier fallback paths when dedicated capacity is saturated.
- High-frequency asks: cost visibility per-route, KV/prefix pre-warming API, explicit model-variant pinning per-route, and a small set of SDK hooks for batching hints.
- Quick-wins (customer-impactful, low-effort): expose per-request metadata in usage logs, add a toggle to disable streaming for a route, surface last-deployed model version in console.

Top 5 emergent asks (ranked by frequency + customer impact):
1) Predictable latency SLOs + graceful fallback policies
   - Why: multiple enterprise customers reported production incidents when Dedicated pools hit capacity; app logic had to implement brittle retries.
   - Ask: an ops-configurable policy that routes to a lower-cost compatible model or to Hosted with preserved auth headers and telemetry.
   - Risk: needs infra coordination (routing + auth), and a clear UX for what “compatible” means.

2) KV/Prefix pre-warm / cache control API
   - Why: customers with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) workflows lose 50–200ms on cold-start KV cache misses; many want programmatic pre-warm at rollout or scale-up events.
   - Ask: API to push/prime keys and optionally reserve cache capacity for a given customer pool.
   - Quick probe: add a REST endpoint that accepts key prefixes + TTL and returns priming status.

3) Per-route cost & token visibility + spend alerts
   - Why: product teams want to map business features to token spend and set automated alerts when a route exceeds an allocated budget.
   - Ask: per-route daily/weekly spend breakdown + webhook alerts and simple budget enforcement (soft block or notify).

4) SDK batching hints + simpler continuous-batching controls
   - Why: some startups saw 20–30% cost reduction if they could nudge the runtime about latency tolerance for specific calls (e.g., background scoring jobs vs. user-facing chat).
   - Ask: tiny SDK additions: latency_hint (ms), priority (high/normal/low), and a route-level default.

5) Model variant pinning and safe rollouts by quality metric
   - Why: customers are conservative about switching to quantized or distilled variants. They want gradual rollouts tied to prompt-set quality checks (not just latency).
   - Ask: rollout config that routes X% of traffic to variant B and automatically pauses or rolls back if eval drift exceeds threshold.

Representative vignettes (short):
- Fintech customer (large private deployment): "We need an emergency fallback when our Dedicated GPUs run out — our reconciliation pipeline stalls otherwise." (Jira: JIRA-CS-9812)
- Marketplace startup: "We wished we could heat the cache before peak morning traffic — customers saw answer flicker for ~90s after a deploy."
- Health app: "We can’t show tokenized cost per feature to our finance owners — opaque billing is blocking a PO."

Low-effort items we can ship quickly (impact vs. dev rough estimate):
- Surface last-deployed model version per route in Console (impact: high, effort: small).
- Add per-request metadata field to usage logs for customer-provided route-tags (impact: high, effort: small).
- Route toggle to disable streaming response delivery (impact: medium, effort: small).
- Expose KV cache hit/miss rate in observability for the last 24h (impact: medium, effort: small-medium).

Mid-term proposals (3–6 months):
- Fallback policy engine: infra + console + audit trail. Must include compatibility matrix and a visible dry-run mode.
- Cost-per-route budgets with webhook actions: allow teams to set soft alerts, hard throttles, or automated throttling to a cheaper model.
- Eval-driven rollout: tie canarying to automated evals for a specified prompt set. Requires eval infra + metric store + console UX for thresholds.

Quality/regression signals customers are asking for:
- Prompt-set pass/fail rates (example: 120 golden prompts; require >= 98% pass to continue rollout).
- Latency distribution per model variant (by seq_len buckets).
- Token-level quality drift alerts (integrated with Redwood Optimize).

Engineering constraints & notes (from infra sync):
- Routing fallback requires auth & observability plumbing to preserve attribution.
- Pre-warm API may need quota guardrails to prevent cache priming storms. Suggest rate-limiting + audit logs.
- Per-route billing granularity exists but the console & retention policies need work to make it useful to customers.

Open questions / unresolved tradeoffs:
- Should fallback to Hosted count as billable to customer’s Dedicated contract or be billed separately? (legal + sales)
- How to define model 'compatibility' programmatically (same family? same tokenizer? max_seq_len?)
- What guardrails for pre-warm to avoid denial-of-cache attacks?

Proposed next steps (who does what):
- CS: run 2 quick 30-min customer interviews with top-tier clients (assigned: Miguel) — goal: validate fallback policy acceptance criteria (by 2026-11-30).
- Product: draft PRD for "Fallback Policy Engine" that includes compatibility matrix and audit trail (owner: Priya) — spike due 2026-12-15.
- Infra: prototype a minimal KV pre-warm endpoint and rate limit behavior (owner: Evan) — spike demo 2026-12-08.
- Growth & Sales: prepare a brief explaining billing choices and recommended default (owner: Mara) — sync once PRD exists.

Notes to self / loose fragments:
- Consider a simple consent/ack in Dedicated contracts for occasional Hosted fallback to remove billing ambiguity.
- Explore a small "pre-warm credits" token for customers who need warm caches before traffic.
- Small UX: show "Cache health" badge in Console that warns when miss-rate > threshold after deploy.

Appendix: raw customer quote snippets (unedited)
- "We saw a spike where every request reloaded the same few embedding keys — our users got duplicate content for a minute."
- "If I could set a 60s window to pre-warm the cache at deploy time we'd be fine."
- "Show me per-feature cost and I can justify doubling our usage."

If anything here should be escalated to GTM or Legal immediately, flag in Slack #cs-escalations. Otherwise this stays as a working draft for the next CS -> Product sync.

-- Aisha
